correctness.rationale: The two deleted-edge incidence types exhaust all pairs up to relabelling. On either graph, for each surviving color lineage in the universal clique, its next color depends only on its current color, the exact states of the fault endpoints, and whether any twin is excited. A resting twin cannot itself be that excited witness. All copies of an initial twin color thus follow the same lineage. Keeping one labelled representative of every initial color preserves state equality at every pair of times in both directions, even if lineages merge. The reduction does not merely classify cycles in the quotient by the current unordered support. I independently built neighbor sets and computed the first t with F^(t+3)(s)=F^t(s) for every one of the 189 and 567 endpoint/support representatives. Such a t was always found by 4; the period is 1 if the state is fixed and 3 otherwise. First equality at distance 3 is first periodic entry because any eventual period divides 3. All ten support triples in each family matched. For support coefficient triple (c,d,e) and r fault endpoints, the exact coefficients of (1,2^n,3^n) are (c-2d+3e,(d-3e)/2^r,e/3^r) by surjection counts; this independently matches every reported formula. Direct full-state enumeration at n=5,6,7 also agreed. The (0,3) counts divided by three imply the two-orbit difference, and summing period-one cells gives the six-state extinction difference. The nonzero singleton-support counts at t=4 ensure sharpness for every allowed n. At the excluded n=4 disjoint boundary the labelled word (1,0,0,2) has least period four, independently confirming the exception.
residual_risks: The direct full-state checks are finite corroboration; the exact lineage reduction and support weighting justify all n. The result gives no per-orbit basin counts or classification for other defect patterns or update rules.

value.rationale: These exhaust the two ways of imposing the same smallest nontrivial edge-incidence comparison on a dense clique. Exact conditioning on the least period and first-entry clock finds a redistribution at maximal latency and a constant difference in orbit and extinction counts invisible to edge count. The finite lineage reduction is an explicit all-order mechanism for obtaining these sharp counts, not a fit at small n.
residual_risks: The comparison is deterministic and specific to the two defects and three-state threshold-one rule; it does not quantify generic perturbation resilience.
